sentences.show: A chemist made a new molecule, then left it on a shelf for five years.
Albert Hofmann first made LSD on this day in 1938.
He worked for Sandoz, in Basel, studying ergot, a fungus that grows on rye.
He hoped for a medicine for breathing and circulation. It was set aside.
In April 1943, he made it again, and accidentally absorbed a tiny amount.
Three days later, he took what he thought was a small dose. It was about ten times the amount needed.
He asked his assistant to take him home. As was usual in Basel, they went by bicycle.
That ride is now known as Bicycle Day.
It spread far beyond the lab. In 1965, Sandoz stopped making it.
Hofmann lived to 102. He believed his discovery had been misused.
Also on this day: Sweden's king fell at Lützen, and Artemis One launched.
